name: Trusted-forwarder open relay approval drain
summary: Forwarder 0x26bbc304699d31b5b3accfa83320a1a396da01f9 accepted an arbitrary claimed sender, appended that address to caller-supplied calldata, and called an arbitrary target without authenticating a signature or caller. The attacker claimed to be each approval holder and routed through a receiver that trusted this forwarder, causing its spending helper and the shared AllowanceTarget to transfer approved aUSDT, USDT and stETH balances.
notes: The receiver installed implementation 0xc5107fc88af7a0536f9197cfc68fc86fd60ed846 for selector 0xaced3248. That implementation hardcodes 0x26bbc304699d31b5b3accfa83320a1a396da01f9 as its trusted forwarder, making the forwarder's unauthenticated claimed-sender path usable against standing AllowanceTarget approvals.

The receipt shows the drain of 85,744.811604 aUSDT, 69,140.278477 USDT and 32.517352764402807668 stETH from seven approval holders. The aUSDT was redeemed and the stETH was liquidated with the rest of the basket; the attack contract then transferred exactly 229,030.971300 USDT to the attacker EOA. This exact realised-proceeds net measurement avoids imposing a spot price on the stETH disposal. Gas is not deducted and no recovery is netted.
The exact figure is the attacker's realised USDT proceeds rather than a gross incident-time mark of the aUSDT, USDT and stETH victim basket.
Review replaces the seed row's a152 proxy target with the unauthenticated forwarder and treats installation of the receiver implementation that hardcoded trust in it as the causal reset.
